newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek inflation seen below 5.0pct by end 97-min.
newsitem.headline: Greek inflation seen below 5.0pct by end 97-min.

text.p: Greek National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou said CPI inflation would fall below 5.0 percent by end-1997 and the country would satisfy the Maastricht criteria for EMU membership at end-1998.
"...inflation will have fallen below 5.0 percent by year-end," said Papandoniou. ".. at end-1998, we will have fulfilled the convergence criteria.."
He was speaking after EU commissioner for regional policies and cohesion Monika Wulf-Mathies who presented the EU report on economic and social cohesion.
Revised consumer price inflation fell to 6.8 percent year-on-year in January from 7.3 percent in December 1996.
Greece's average inflation stood at 8.5 percent in 1996 and is projected to drop to 6.5 percent in 1997.

The general government budget deficit decreased to an estimated 7.6 percent of GDP in 1996 from 9.1 percent in 1995. It is projected to fall further to 4.2 percent of GDP in 1997 and 2.4 percent in 1998.
But the debt to GDP ratio was estimated at 110.7 percent in 1996 and is forecast at 113.4 percent in 1997. The debt to GDP Maastricht criteria calls for that ratio to be below 60 percent.
Greece does not issue or auction long-term government bonds currently so that no comparison can be made with EU average long-term rates.
